questions.stem: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) introduced PANCHAYATI RAJ as a CONSTITUTIONAL institution, adding:
questions.explanation: 73RD CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT ACT, 1992 (effective 24 April 1993) — gave PANCHAYATI RAJ (rural local self-government) CONSTITUTIONAL status. PART IX (Articles 243-243O) inserted. Also added 11TH SCHEDULE listing 29 FUNCTIONAL SUBJECTS that states may DEVOLVE to Panchayats (agriculture, land reforms, rural housing, drinking water, roads, poverty alleviation, primary education, health, etc.) — not mandatory, states have discretion. KEY FEATURES: (1) 3-TIER STRUCTURE — (a) Village level — GRAM PANCHAYAT; (b) Intermediate/block level — PANCHAYAT SAMITI (states with population > 20 lakh must have intermediate tier); (c) District level — ZILLA PARISHAD. (2) GRAM SABHA — general body of ALL REGISTERED VOTERS in the village; village 'assembly' as grassroots democratic body. (3) DIRECT ELECTIONS for all seats at all 3 levels. (4) RESERVATION: (a) 1/3 seats for WOMEN; (b) SC/ST seats proportional to state population; (c) Women + SC/ST reservations intersect (so 1/3 within SC/ST too). Many states have since increased to 50% WOMEN reservation (Bihar 2006 first; 21+ states now). Rotation of reserved seats. (5) 5-YEAR TERM for all Panchayat bodies. (6) STATE ELECTION COMMISSION (SEC) — separate from ECI — to conduct Panchayat + municipal elections (Art 243K). (7) STATE FINANCE COMMISSION (every 5 years) — recommends financial resource-sharing (Art 243I). (8) AUDIT + accounts. (9) DISQUALIFICATIONS + other provisions. 74TH CAA 1992 — parallel amendment for URBAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT (Nagar Palikas / Municipal Corporations / Councils); PART IXA (243P-243ZG) + 12TH SCHEDULE (18 subjects). 3-tier urban: Municipal Corporations (big cities, >10 lakh pop) + Municipal Councils/Municipalities (100K-10 lakh) + Nagar Panchayats (<100K transitional). DEVOLUTION varies widely by state; Kerala + Karnataka = most devolved; UP, Bihar = weak. HISTORICAL ROOTS: (1) Indian village councils ancient (Uttiramerur inscriptions); (2) Balwant Rai Mehta Committee 1957 — first recommended 3-tier; (3) Rajasthan was first state to implement Panchayati Raj (2 Oct 1959, Nagaur by Nehru); (4) Ashok Mehta Committee 1978 — 2-tier; (5) L.M. Singhvi 1986 — constitutional status; (6) 64th + 65th CABs 1989 (Rajiv Gandhi) — introduced, failed in RS; (7) finally 73rd + 74th CAAs by NARASIMHA RAO govt 1992. 29 subjects transferable to Panchayats.

questions.stem: RAJASTHAN became the FIRST state to implement the 3-tier Panchayati Raj system. Inaugurated by Nehru at:
questions.explanation: PANCHAYATI RAJ in India — formally inaugurated by PM JAWAHARLAL NEHRU on 2 OCTOBER 1959 (GANDHI JAYANTI) at NAGAUR district of RAJASTHAN. Rajasthan became the FIRST state to implement 3-tier Panchayati Raj. ANDHRA PRADESH followed soon after (1959). BACKGROUND: (1) BALWANT RAI MEHTA COMMITTEE (1957) — set up by Nehru govt to examine working of COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT Programme (launched 1952, 2 Oct) + NATIONAL EXTENSION SERVICE (1953). Found that rural development required DEMOCRATIC DECENTRALISATION. Key recommendations: (a) establish 3-TIER Panchayati Raj structure (Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti → Zilla Parishad); (b) DIRECT elections at village level; (c) indirect at higher levels; (d) executive body; (e) 5-year tenure. (2) NEHRU'S ENTHUSIASTIC adoption + launch. (3) Followed by other states gradually. EVOLUTION: (1) 1950s-60s — EARLY ADOPTION; enthusiasm. (2) 1970s — DECLINE — central schemes bypassed Panchayats; political neglect. (3) ASHOK MEHTA COMMITTEE (1977-78, Janata) — recommended 2-tier (Zilla + Mandal Panchayat); INSTITUTIONALISE through Constitutional amendment. (4) G.V.K. RAO COMMITTEE (1985). (5) L.M. SINGHVI COMMITTEE (1986) — recommended CONSTITUTIONAL RECOGNITION. (6) 64th + 65th CABs (1989) by Rajiv Gandhi — failed in RS. (7) 73rd + 74th CAAs (1992) by Narasimha Rao govt — SUCCESSFUL. KARNATAKA's ZILLA PARISHAD Act 1983 was path-breaking — Ramakrishna Hegde-led Janata Dal govt first gave substantive powers + funds to ZP. GANDHI's DREAM of 'GRAM SWARAJ' (village self-rule) — Panchayati Raj realises it partially; Gandhi envisaged VILLAGES as 'little republics'. Ambedkar was critical — 'what is a village but a sink of localism, den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness + communalism'. Indian Panchayati Raj tries to reconcile BOTH views — grassroots democracy + protection of minorities + welfare planning. STATUS (2024): ~2.6 lakh Panchayats; ~31 LAKH elected representatives at panchayat level (LARGEST DEMOCRATIC DEVOLUTION in world); 13+ LAKH WOMEN representatives (with 1/3 quota; some states 50%). based on recommendations of Balwant Rai Mehta Committee 1957.

questions.stem: The 3-tier PANCHAYATI RAJ structure for rural areas consists of:

options.option_text: Gram Sabha → Nagar Palika → Municipal Corporation
GRAM PANCHAYAT (village) → PANCHAYAT SAMITI (block) → ZILLA PARISHAD (district)
Nyaya Panchayat → Gram Panchayat → District Panchayat

questions.explanation: 3-TIER PANCHAYATI RAJ SYSTEM (per 73rd CAA): (1) GRAM PANCHAYAT (Village level) — covers village(s) with ~500+ population typically; headed by SARPANCH (Pradhan in UP, Mukhiya in Bihar, Ward Member in some); DIRECTLY ELECTED by Gram Sabha; 5-year term. Elected members of Gram Panchayat are called WARD MEMBERS / PANCHS. GRAM SABHA — general body of ALL REGISTERED VOTERS in the village; meets at least 2-4 times/year; discusses + approves GP budget, plans; 'GENERAL ASSEMBLY'. (2) PANCHAYAT SAMITI (intermediate/block level, also called MANDAL PANCHAYAT in KA, JANPAD PANCHAYAT in MP-CG, BLOCK PANCHAYAT in Kerala, KSHETRA PANCHAYAT in UP) — covers a block / tehsil; headed by PRADHAN / CHAIRMAN / BLOCK PRESIDENT. Members DIRECTLY elected (per 73rd CAA); Sarpanches of GPs also ex-officio members. Executes block-level schemes. Intermediate tier is MANDATORY only for states with population >20 LAKH; small states (Goa, NE) may skip. (3) ZILLA PARISHAD (District level, also called DISTRICT PANCHAYAT, DDC in J&K) — covers district; headed by ADHYAKSHA / ZILLA PRAMUKH / DP Chairperson. Members directly elected; PS Pradhans + MPs + MLAs from district ex-officio members (non-voting). Executes district planning + coordinating role. OFFICIALS ASSOCIATED: (1) CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER (CEO) / Additional CEO of Zilla Parishad — IAS officer; day-to-day admin. (2) BLOCK DEVELOPMENT OFFICER (BDO) — at block level, state civil service officer, coordinates Panchayat Samiti work + govt schemes (MGNREGA, PMAY-G, Swachh Bharat-G etc.). (3) VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT OFFICER / Gram Vikas Adhikari at GP level. Panchayat Secretary = GP's record-keeper. FUNCTIONS (per 11th Schedule, 29 items): agriculture, minor irrigation, watershed, animal husbandry, fishery, social forestry, small scale industries, khadi, rural housing, drinking water, rural electrification, non-conventional energy, poverty alleviation, primary + secondary education, adult education, libraries, health + sanitation, family welfare, women + child welfare, Panchayat markets, fairs, SC/ST welfare, public distribution, etc. IMPLEMENTATION VARIES widely by state — KERALA + KARNATAKA devolve ~60%+ functions/funds; UP-BIHAR < 30%.

questions.stem: The 74th CAA (1992) constituted URBAN LOCAL BODIES in THREE types, based on city size:

options.option_text: MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (large cities), MUNICIPAL COUNCIL/MUNICIPALITY (medium), NAGAR PANCHAYAT
Zilla Parishad, Panchayat Samiti, Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: 74TH CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT ACT, 1992 — parallel to 73rd; gave URBAN LOCAL BODIES constitutional status. PART IXA (Arts 243P-243ZG) + 12TH SCHEDULE (18 subjects). 3 TYPES of Urban Local Bodies (based on population + characteristics, determined by state Governors): (1) MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (MAHA NAGAR PALIKA) — for LARGER URBAN AREAS (generally >10 lakh / 1 million, varies by state). Headed by MAYOR (elected by Corporators in most; direct election in some states). CEO = MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER (IAS officer). Examples: BMC (Mumbai — Asia's largest), MCD (Delhi; tripartite + unified 2022 as single MCD), Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Chennai Municipal Corporation, BBMP (Bengaluru), GHMC (Hyderabad), PMC (Pune), NMMC (Navi Mumbai), NDMC (New Delhi, sep. Council). (2) MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / MUNICIPALITY / NAGAR PARISHAD / NAGAR PALIKA — for MEDIUM-sized towns (1 lakh to 10 lakh approx). Headed by CHAIRPERSON / PRESIDENT. CEO = CHIEF MUNICIPAL OFFICER. (3) NAGAR PANCHAYAT (TRANSITIONAL area) — for AREAS IN TRANSITION from rural to urban (typically < 1 lakh population). Headed by President. STRUCTURE COMMON TO ALL 3: (1) WARDS — basic unit; DIRECT ELECTIONS. (2) WARDS COMMITTEES mandatory in cities with population > 3 lakh (Art 243S). (3) RESERVATION: 1/3 seats for WOMEN; SC/ST proportional; OBC (enabling provision — state discretion). (4) TERM: 5 years. (5) STATE ELECTION COMMISSION conducts elections. (6) STATE FINANCE COMMISSION (Art 243Y) recommends resource-sharing. (7) METROPOLITAN PLANNING COMMITTEES (Art 243ZE) for 10 lakh+ cities. (8) DISTRICT PLANNING COMMITTEES (Art 243ZD). 12TH SCHEDULE SUBJECTS (18): urban planning, regulation of land use, roads + bridges, water supply, public health + sanitation + solid waste management, fire services, urban forestry, environment, safeguards of weaker sections, slum improvement, urban poverty alleviation, public amenities (parks, gardens, playgrounds), promotion of culture + heritage, burials + cremations, cattle pounds + animal care, registration of births + deaths, street lights, public conveniences (toilets), etc. 74th CAA urban devolution is generally MORE COMPLETE than 73rd rural in most states — cities have stronger tax base (property tax, commercial tax). Part IXA; 12th Schedule 18 subjects; transitional small.

questions.stem: The MAHATMA GANDHI NATIONAL RURAL EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE ACT (MGNREGA) 2005 GUARANTEES:

options.option_text: 100 DAYS of guaranteed wage employment per FINANCIAL YEAR to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for UNSKILLED MANUAL WORK
Permanent govt jobs for rural youth

questions.explanation: MGNREGA (originally NREGA — NATIONAL RURAL EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE ACT, 2005; renamed MAHATMA GANDHI NREGA in 2009). Passed on 25 August 2005 (UPA-I, Manmohan Singh); effective from 2 Feb 2006 (initially 200 districts). FLAGSHIP rights-based social security scheme — WORLD's LARGEST public employment programme. GUARANTEES: UP TO 100 DAYS of guaranteed WAGE EMPLOYMENT per financial year, to EVERY RURAL household whose ADULT members volunteer for UNSKILLED MANUAL WORK. WAGE: state-wise, linked to CPI-AL (agricultural labour), revised annually. Current wage range ~₹240-370/day (varies by state). KEY FEATURES: (1) DEMAND-DRIVEN: if work not provided within 15 DAYS of demand, UNEMPLOYMENT ALLOWANCE payable (though states often default). (2) 1/3 beneficiaries must be WOMEN — consistently achieved (women ~54% of person-days). (3) WAGES paid via bank/post office account; DIRECT BENEFIT TRANSFER. (4) Work within 5 KM RADIUS of village; else EXTRA wages. (5) WORKSITE amenities — water, shade, first-aid, creche if 5+ children. (6) 60:40 ratio of LABOUR to MATERIAL cost in works. (7) WORKS categories: water conservation (ponds, check dams — 60%+ of works), land development, rural roads, afforestation, sanitation (SBM toilets), individual assets for SC/ST/BPL (well, irrigation, housing plinth). (8) SOCIAL AUDIT — mandatory by Gram Sabha. ADMINISTRATION: (a) Centrally funded (90% Centre, 10% state for Labour; 75:25 for material). (b) Planned + executed by 3-tier PRI system — GP plans + executes, PS supervises, ZP coordinates. (c) Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) at Centre; State Rural Development Dept. ACHIEVEMENTS: ~7-10 crore households employed each year; ~250-300 crore person-days annually; ₹85,000+ crore annual budget. CRITIQUES: (a) leakages + ghost entries — (Aadhaar + DBT + Geotag of works + Citizen Information Boards + MIS introduced to reduce); (b) delayed payments; (c) states overdraw + Centre plays catch-up; (d) 'jobless growth' dependency — desirable or not?; (e) quality of assets variable. DURING COVID-19 (2020-22), MGNREGA proved a LIFE-LINE — 7.5 crore households worked (highest ever) as migrants returned. MGNREGA linked to other schemes: PMAY-G housing, NRLM livelihoods, SBM-G toilets, DDU-GKY skilling.
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: Elected governing body of the village
General body of ALL REGISTERED VOTERS of a village/panchayat area

questions.explanation: GRAM SABHA — 'VILLAGE ASSEMBLY' = GENERAL BODY of ALL REGISTERED VOTERS of a village / GROUP of villages forming a Gram Panchayat area. DEFINED under Article 243(b) of Constitution + state panchayati raj acts. STRUCTURE: (1) All adults (18+) registered as voters in the electoral roll of the village panchayat area = MEMBERS of Gram Sabha; (2) MEETS AT LEAST 2-4 TIMES per year (states vary — many now mandate QUARTERLY meetings); (3) quorum usually 1/10 of members (or 100 persons, whichever lower). FUNCTIONS / POWERS: (1) APPROVE Gram Panchayat ANNUAL BUDGET + PLAN; (2) RECEIVES annual accounts + audit reports; (3) IDENTIFIES BENEFICIARIES of govt schemes (PMAY-G houses, MGNREGA wagework, Ayushman Bharat cards, ration cards); (4) SOCIAL AUDIT of GP works; (5) approves implementation of certain projects; (6) reviews functioning of institutions (schools, Anganwadis, PHCs); (7) in SCHEDULED AREAS (PESA Act 1996), enhanced powers re: land alienation, minor forest produce, minor minerals, planning. GRAM SABHA is DIRECT DEMOCRACY — every voter participates directly, not through representative. Different from GRAM PANCHAYAT (elected members body). PESA ACT (Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act, 1996) — extends Part IX to 5TH SCHEDULE tribal areas with MODIFICATIONS. States covered: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana. UNIQUE GRAM SABHA POWERS in PESA: (1) consultation MANDATORY on land acquisition; (2) consent required for minor mineral prospecting + granting of concessions; (3) ownership of MINOR FOREST PRODUCE (tendu, mahua, honey, gum, lac); (4) control over money-lending to STs; (5) control over local markets; (6) consultation on welfare schemes. PESA aims to secure SELF-GOVERNANCE for tribal communities. IMPLEMENTATION PATCHY though — forest rights still contested (Forest Rights Act 2006 overlapping), mining clearances often bypass Gram Sabha. Supreme Court's NIYAMGIRI JUDGMENT (2013, Dongria Kondh vs Vedanta) upheld Gram Sabhas' right to reject bauxite mining. SAMATA v. AP (1997) similarly. Gram Sabha is the FUNDAMENTAL DEMOCRATIC UNIT envisaged by Constitution makers — a realisation of Gandhian 'Gram Swaraj'. decision-making + oversight body, mandated to meet at least 2-4 times/year.

questions.stem: The BALWANT RAI MEHTA COMMITTEE (1957) recommended:

options.option_text: Introduction of 3-TIER PANCHAYATI RAJ with direct election at village level + indirect at higher

questions.explanation: BALWANT RAI MEHTA COMMITTEE (1957) — officially 'Committee on Plan Projects' / 'Team on Community Projects + National Extension Service'. Chaired by BALWANT RAI G. MEHTA (Gujarat Congress leader, later CM of Gujarat). ORIGIN: set up by PLANNING COMMISSION to evaluate working of COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (CDP, launched 2 Oct 1952) + NATIONAL EXTENSION SERVICE (NES, 1953) — both flagship rural development schemes of Nehru era. FINDINGS: CDP + NES had FAILED to develop rural India effectively; reasons included: (a) lack of PEOPLE'S PARTICIPATION; (b) TOP-DOWN bureaucracy-driven approach; (c) weak LOCAL INSTITUTIONS. KEY RECOMMENDATIONS (submitted Nov 1957): (1) 3-TIER PANCHAYATI RAJ structure — (a) GRAM PANCHAYAT (village level — directly elected); (b) PANCHAYAT SAMITI (block level — indirectly elected from GP sarpanches + elected officials); (c) ZILLA PARISHAD (district level — indirectly). Hence 'DEMOCRATIC DECENTRALISATION'. (2) PANCHAYAT SAMITI to be EXECUTIVE body, responsible for development. (3) ZP to be ADVISORY + COORDINATING. (4) SHIFT RURAL PROGRAMMES to Panchayats. (5) 5-YEAR tenure. RESULT: NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL accepted recommendations; RAJASTHAN became FIRST state to implement (Nehru inaugurated at NAGAUR, 2 Oct 1959). ANDHRA PRADESH followed soon after. By mid-1960s ~15 states implemented. LATER COMMITTEES: (1) ASHOK MEHTA COMMITTEE (1977-78, Janata govt) — recommended 2-TIER (Zilla Parishad + Mandal Panchayat) with ZP as focal; ASSIGNED development planning to ZP; ELECTED to all posts; allowed political parties to contest; separate FINANCE for rural local bodies. (2) G.V.K. RAO COMMITTEE (1985) — 'Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development + Poverty Alleviation'; recommended ZP as STRONGEST unit; make DISTRICT COLLECTOR accountable to ZP (controversial; not adopted). (3) L.M. SINGHVI COMMITTEE (1986) — 'Revitalisation of PRIs for Democracy + Development'; CONSTITUTIONAL recognition of PRIs; regular + free elections; adequate resources; NYAYA PANCHAYATS (judicial panchayats) for rural justice. (4) Sarkaria Commission inputs. Implementation came via 73rd CAA 1992 under NARASIMHA RAO govt — 35 YEARS after Balwant Rai Mehta's original recommendations. adopted by Rajasthan + AP in 1959.

questions.stem: STATE ELECTION COMMISSION for conducting panchayat + municipal elections was made a CONSTITUTIONAL body under:
questions.explanation: STATE ELECTION COMMISSION (SEC) — CONSTITUTIONAL body for RURAL + URBAN local body elections in each state. DISTINCT FROM ECI (Election Commission of India, Art 324) which handles Parliament + State Legislature + Presidential/VP polls only. PROVISIONS: (1) Art 243K (inserted by 73rd CAA 1992) — SEC for Panchayat elections. (2) Art 243ZA (inserted by 74th CAA 1992) — SEC for Municipal elections. (3) SINGLE SEC usually handles BOTH rural + urban in each state. (4) STRUCTURE: One member — the STATE ELECTION COMMISSIONER — appointed by the GOVERNOR. Term 5 years typically. (5) INDEPENDENCE: Commissioner can be removed only in MANNER + on GROUNDS of a HIGH COURT judge — ensures security of tenure. (6) FUNCTIONS: (a) superintendence, direction + control of preparation of electoral rolls for panchayat + ULB elections; (b) conduct of elections; (c) delimitation of wards + constituencies (in some states); (d) resolution of election disputes. (7) STATE LEGISLATURE makes laws regulating elections to panchayats + ULBs (subject to Constitution). KEY ISSUE: SEC conducts local polls INDEPENDENTLY but powers + authority often UNDERMINED by state govts in practice. RECENT CONFLICTS: (1) MAHARASHTRA 2021-22 — OBC reservation in local body elections dispute between state + SC led to delays; SEC caught in middle. (2) WEST BENGAL Panchayat 2023 — controversial poll marred by violence; SEC Rajiva Sinha's role criticised. (3) ANDHRA PRADESH 2020 — Gram Panchayat election delayed by state vs SEC Nimmagadda Ramesh Kumar legal battle; SC intervened + backed SEC. (4) BIHAR, KERALA, KARNATAKA — OBC reservation + delimitation issues. SC has REPEATEDLY reiterated SEC's INDEPENDENCE — Kishansingh Tomar (2006), Anugrah Narayan Singh (2007), Suresh Mahajan (2022). DELIMITATION: separate STATE DELIMITATION COMMISSION may also exist for ward delineation in states. ECI is distinct — conducts Parliament + Legislative Assembly + Presidential/VP elections; 3-member (CEC + 2 ECs, since 1993); headquartered at Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi. STATE Finance Commission (Art 243I / 243Y) — separate — recommends finance-sharing between state + local bodies every 5 years. separate from ECI; one Commissioner appointed by Governor; municipalities.

questions.stem: Which state has the HIGHEST percentage of WOMEN representation in Panchayats (often >50%)?

options.option_text: BIHAR was the FIRST state to legislate 50% women reservation (2006); now 21+ states have 50%

questions.explanation: WOMEN in PANCHAYATS — 73rd CAA mandated 1/3 (33%) reservation for women. Many states voluntarily RAISED to 50% (1/2) under enabling power in Art 243D(3). TIMELINE: (1) BIHAR — FIRST state to raise to 50% (2006, under Nitish Kumar). (2) Then: UTTARAKHAND, MADHYA PRADESH, HIMACHAL PRADESH, KERALA, ODISHA, RAJASTHAN, TRIPURA, MAHARASHTRA, ANDHRA PRADESH, ASSAM, CHHATTISGARH, GUJARAT, JHARKHAND, KARNATAKA, PUNJAB, SIKKIM, TAMIL NADU, TELANGANA, UTTAR PRADESH (2015 under SP govt — yes, UP has 50%), WEST BENGAL, GOA. (3) About 21 STATES + UTs have 50% women reservation in Panchayats. STATUS (Ministry of Panchayati Raj 2024 data): ~14.5 LAKH ELECTED WOMEN REPRESENTATIVES out of ~31 lakh total PRI reps = ~46-47% women overall. 6 states are >50% women. ACROSS STATES: (a) KARNATAKA ~55% women; (b) JHARKHAND, MP, CHHATTISGARH, ODISHA > 50%; (c) Kerala, HP, Rajasthan > 50%; (d) UP, Bihar ~50%; (e) Maharashtra 50%. INDIA has the WORLD's LARGEST women's political representation at local level. IMPACT studies: (1) LORI BEAMAN, ESTHER DUFLO et al. — studies of quota-based women leaders → more investment in drinking water, health, roads; less corruption; more complaints registered; erosion of caste-based patriarchy; role models. (2) CONCEPT of 'SARPANCH PATI' / 'Mukhiya Pati' — proxy politics where husband wields actual power behind elected wife — STILL PREVALENT in many areas. State initiatives to address: training programmes for elected women reps, Mahila Sabha (parallel women's body), direct bank accounts. (3) 'MAHILA PANCHAYATS' in Delhi, Mumbai — Nari Adalat type informal judicial bodies. WORLD COMPARISON: India's ~46% women in local govt = BEST IN WORLD in absolute sense (~14.5 lakh women leaders). For perspective: US has ~0.5 lakh women local reps; EU ~30% women in local councils. PROGRESSIVE features also include: (a) rotation of reserved seats; (b) reservation within SC/ST category; (c) OBC sub-quotas in many states. NATIONAL PANCHAYATI RAJ DAY = 24 APRIL (date 73rd CAA came into force, 1993). PANCHAYATS are 'CRADLES OF DEMOCRACY' per Gandhi + first PM Nehru. Kerala, Odisha, MP, Rajasthan, HP, Tripura, etc.

questions.stem: PESA ACT 1996 (Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas) extends Panchayati Raj to:
questions.explanation: PESA ACT 1996 (PANCHAYATS [Extension to Scheduled Areas] Act, 24 Dec 1996) — extends the provisions of Part IX (73rd CAA Panchayati Raj) to the 5TH SCHEDULE AREAS with CRITICAL MODIFICATIONS for tribal governance. COVERS 10 STATES (as of 2024, Telangana added after bifurcation): ANDHRA PRADESH, CHHATTISGARH, GUJARAT, HIMACHAL PRADESH, JHARKHAND, MADHYA PRADESH, MAHARASHTRA, ODISHA, RAJASTHAN, TELANGANA. NOT applicable to 6th SCHEDULE areas of NE (Assam Hill Areas, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram — which have their OWN Autonomous District Councils). DEVELOPED based on BHURIA COMMITTEE (1994-95) recommendations. KEY FEATURES: (1) GRAM SABHA (not GP) is PRINCIPAL INSTITUTION in PESA areas; far stronger powers than elsewhere. (2) GRAM SABHA approves village plans + beneficiaries; socioeconomic planning. (3) CONSULTATION with Gram Sabha MANDATORY BEFORE: (a) LAND ACQUISITION for development; (b) acquisition of land for displacement; (c) rehab + resettlement schemes. (4) CONSENT of Gram Sabha required for: (a) prospecting + mining MINOR MINERALS in Scheduled Areas. (5) OWNERSHIP of MINOR FOREST PRODUCE (MFP) — tendu, mahua, honey, lac, wax, etc. — vested in Gram Sabha. (6) MANAGEMENT OF water bodies, minor water resources. (7) Regulation of MONEY-LENDING to STs. (8) Control over LOCAL MARKETS + fairs. (9) Prohibition / regulation of intoxicants. (10) Safeguards of TRIBAL CULTURE + customs. STATE LEGISLATIONS: each state enacts its own PESA Rules. Maharashtra PESA rules 2014 considered progressive; Chhattisgarh's delayed till 2022. IMPACT: (1) IN THEORY — tribals have real power over land + forests + minerals; (2) IN PRACTICE — implementation weak due to (a) mining interests; (b) Forest Rights Act 2006 overlap; (c) bureaucratic resistance; (d) resistance of contractors to Gram Sabha approval. NIYAMGIRI CASE (SC 2013) — Odisha — Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected Vedanta's bauxite mining 12-0 (all 12 Gram Sabhas); SC upheld the Gram Sabha VETO — LANDMARK PESA + FRA win.
